proof.text: For each m≥n, the quotient maps B_{Y,m}→B_{Y,n} and their pullbacks to X and Z give the actual transitions of P_m,Q_m,H_m and of the unit systems. Since P,Q,H are K-flat with flat terms over R_Y, termwise change of rings along R_Y→B_{Y,m} gives K-flat complexes P_m,Q_m,H_m of B_{Y,m}-modules with flat terms [lem-pur-kflat-change-of-rings]; the unit complexes B_{W,m}[0] are of this form with P=R_W. Hence derived change of rings along B_{Y,m}→B_{Y,n} is computed termwise on them [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], and the transition-adjoint α_{m,n} is the canonical associativity isomorphism (P⊗_{R_Y}B_{Y,m})⊗_{B_{Y,m}}B_{Y,n}≅P⊗_{R_Y}B_{Y,n}, and similarly for Q,H and the units. Associativity of tensor and q_{r,n}=q_{m,n}q_{r,m} give τ_{n,n}=1 and the cocycle identity, so these strict quotient towers, viewed in Tow_{R_Y} through Res_n, are normalized DVR towers. By the K-flat total tensor model [lem-pur-kflat-total-tensor-model], Tot(P_n⊗_{B_{Y,n}}Q_n) (and the triple tensors) are K-flat with flat terms and represent the derived tensor of the levels; by exactness of the pro-etale module inverse image along the constant-ring identification f^{-1}B_{Y,n}≅B_{X,n} [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-exact], the termwise f_n^*P_n and h_n^*f_n^*P_n represent the derived pullbacks, and they are again K-flat with flat terms [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-kflat-pullback], so the total tensors of pulled-back complexes also represent derived tensors [lem-pur-kflat-total-tensor-model]. So the strict towers in the statement are models of the fiberwise derived tensor and system inverse image, and the normalized tensor/pullback closure lemma applies: it identifies the transition-adjoint of a tensor with the tensor of the transition-adjoints after the strong monoidal scalar-extension comparison, and the transition-adjoint after pullback with the pulled-back transition-adjoint. Both are therefore invertible, and the total tensors and termwise pullbacks in the statement are normalized coherent systems.

source.place: Tag 07A4, label lemma-pullback-tensor-product, total-complex construction; quotient associativity is written out here

proof.text: Fix n and apply the cochain comparison lemma to the morphism of ringed topoi induced by f_n. Its map is the chain isomorphism c_{f_n;P_n,Q_n} with the stated pure-tensor formula and inverse. Apply its naturality and its compatibility with the usual reassociation to the two parenthesizations of P_n⊗Q_n⊗H_n. The two composites from f_n^*Tot((P_n⊗Q_n)⊗H_n) to Tot(f_n^*P_n⊗(f_n^*Q_n⊗f_n^*H_n)) therefore agree as chain maps. The direct-sum total differential is the one in the tensor-complex definition, so this is an equality before passing to any derived category or limit.

source.place: Tag 07A4, label lemma-pullback-tensor-product, displayed total-complex comparison and its reassociation compatibility

proof.text: At the same level, the signed-symmetry clause of the cochain lemma gives τ_{f_n^*P_n,f_n^*Q_n}c_{f_n;P_n,Q_n}=c_{f_n;Q_n,P_n}f_n^*(τ_{P_n,Q_n}); on a homogeneous tensor it is exactly the sign (-1)^{pq}. Its two unitor clauses give the two unit equations, because the coefficient pullback identifies f_n^*B_{Y,n}[0] with B_{X,n}[0] and the unit maps are the action maps. For composable f_n and h_n, the composition clause of the same lemma, with the canonical adjunction-normalized comparison a_K, is precisely the displayed equation involving c_{(f∘h)_n}, c_{f_n}, and c_{h_n}. Thus all four finite-level coherence equations hold as chain-map equalities.

source.place: Tag 07A4, label lemma-pullback-tensor-product, signed symmetry, action unitors, and composition comparison

proof.text: The final clause of the cochain comparison lemma says that these same formulas on strict quotient towers commute with every transition. Applying it to the towers constructed in Step 1 shows that c_{f_n} and its inverse, all reassociators, action unitors, signed symmetries, and the pullback-composition maps are strict maps of towers. Consequently each finite-level equality from Steps 2 and 3 is one equality in the strict normalized tower category, simultaneously for all n and compatible with every B_{W,m}→B_{W,n}.

source.place: Tag 07A4, label lemma-pullback-tensor-product, final sentence on strict quotient towers and transitions

proof.text: The derived inverse-limit construction is a functor on strict tower maps by the strict-tower homotopy-limit lemma. Applying it to the equal tower maps of Step 4 preserves equality, and applying it to c_{f_n} and its strict inverse produces mutually inverse maps after Rlim. The coherent substitution lemma identifies the limits of the tensor, pullback, unit and composition expressions with the corresponding completed integral operations; it also identifies the limits of the canonical reassociators, unitors, signed symmetries and composition comparisons with the completed structural maps. Therefore the tower equalities give the asserted integral associativity, symmetry, unit and composition equations.

source.place: Tag 0941, label lemma-derived-limit-is-ok, functorial derived limit for strict systems; completed-operation substitution is the stated tower-to-limit identification

proof.text: Finally use the coherent counit/effectivity comparison for every normalized tower: if M=Rlim_m Res_m M_m, then M⊗^L_R A_n≅M_n for every n. Applying this to each expression in Step 5 and using naturality of the counits identifies the reduction of every integral equation with its finite equation, including the quotient-transition maps. The substitution identifications carry these counits to the completed-operation expressions, so the finite equations obtained in Steps 2–4 are exactly the coherent reductions claimed in the statement.

title: Coherence identities on normalized integral comparison towers
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with uniformizer $\varpi$, and composable scheme morphisms $Z\xrightarrow{h}X\xrightarrow{f}Y$ with $\ell$ invertible on all three schemes [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension, def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. For each $W=Z,X,Y$ set $B_{W,n}=(\mathcal O_E/\varpi^n)_W$ on its small pro-etale site and $R_W=\varprojlim_nB_{W,n}$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Let $P,Q,H$ be integer-indexed flat-term K-flat complexes of $R_Y$-modules [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. Put $P_n=P\otimes_{R_Y}B_{Y,n}$, and similarly for $Q_n,H_n$, with their actual quotient maps. Use direct-sum total tensor [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], termwise $f_n^*,h_n^*$ [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image], and the cochain comparison $c_{f_n}$ with formula $s\otimes(x\otimes y)\mapsto(s\otimes x)\otimes(1\otimes y)$ [lem-pur-cochain-pullback-tensor-coherence].

The systems formed from these three quotient towers, the unit systems $B_{W,\bullet}[0]$, total tensor and these pullbacks are normalized coherent systems [def-coef-normalized-dvr-tower]. Their canonical reassociators, action unitors, signed symmetries and adjunction-normalized pullback-composition maps, together with $c_{f_n}$ and its inverse, are strict maps of towers. In this strict tower category the two routes from $f_n^*\operatorname{Tot}((P_n\otimes Q_n)\otimes H_n)$ to $\operatorname{Tot}(f_n^*P_n\otimes(f_n^*Q_n\otimes f_n^*H_n))$ coincide. The symmetry equation is
$$\tau_{f_n^*P_n,f_n^*Q_n}c_{f_n;P_n,Q_n}=c_{f_n;Q_n,P_n}\,f_n^*(\tau_{P_n,Q_n}),\qquad \tau(x\otimes y)=(-1)^{pq}y\otimes x,$$
for $x\in P_n^p,y\in Q_n^q$. The two unit equations use the action maps and $f_n^*B_{Y,n}[0]\cong B_{X,n}[0]$. With $a_K:(f\circ h)_n^*K\cong h_n^*f_n^*K$, the composition equation is
$$ (a_{P_n}\otimes a_{Q_n})c_{(f\circ h)_n;P_n,Q_n}=c_{h_n;f_n^*P_n,f_n^*Q_n}\,h_n^*(c_{f_n;P_n,Q_n})\,a_{\operatorname{Tot}(P_n\otimes Q_n)}.$$
All these equations are equalities of strict tower maps, compatible with every $B_{W,m}\to B_{W,n}$ for $m\ge n$, before localization or inverse limit. After the functorial derived limit [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit], the substitution identifications [lem-pur-completed-operation-tower-substitution] identify their vertices and structural arrows with the corresponding completed-operation expressions. The resulting equations are the integral associativity, signed symmetry, unit and composition equations, and their coherent reductions via [lem-coef-normalized-dvr-effectivity] are the displayed finite equations, including the quotient-transition maps.
